![](images/80/80577a585741748702b61596db84983592ecbc6c01fca78af033bf82dbe62ad2.png)

Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x={e}^{t},\,y={e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t$
from $t=-3$ to $t=1$ (shown above)?
source_solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})={e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)={e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{1}\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{1}{e}^{t}\sqrt{1+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{1}{e}^{t}\sqrt{2+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}
$$
